title: Timebound Entitlement Archival and Audit-Ready Evidence Guideline
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This guideline defines the Timebound Entitlement Archival (TEA) pattern: a reproducible, auditable process for snapshotting, signing, retaining, and presenting role and entitlement state for a bounded time horizon. TEA ensures that audits, legal requests, and post-incident investigations can reconstruct exactly which identities had which permissions at a specific moment in time.

Scope:

- Applies to all production identity and entitlement systems managed by Redwood Inference (IAM, SSO, provisioners, SCIM connectors, and internal service-role mapping tables).
- Covers ephemeral and long-lived entitlements, service accounts, OAuth client grants, and delegated admin roles.
- Does NOT replace primary log retention policies; it augments audit evidence with frozen, verifiable snapshots optimized for compliance inquiries.

Definitions:

- Entitlement snapshot: an immutable export representing the mapping of principals -> roles/permissions at a given timestamp.
- Timebound entitlement: any permission set that is asserted to be valid for a defined time window (start/end or point-in-time).
- Evidence bundle: signed archive containing entitlement snapshots, related audit events, signature metadata, and provenance manifest.

Goals and Principles:

1) Determinism: Every snapshot generation must be reproducible from recorded inputs.
2) Immutability: Snapshots are content-addressed, signed, and stored in an immutable store (WORM or object-store lifecycle with write-once semantics).
3) Minimum-necessary retention: Keep evidence for the period required by regulators and contract SLAs while anonymizing ephemeral personal identifiers when permitted.
4) Fast produceability: Generating an evidence bundle for a date must be possible within the SLA defined below.

SLOs and Operational Targets:

- Evidence generation SLA: 95% of requests for a day-level snapshot must return a complete evidence bundle within 4 hours; emergency requests (security incident) within 1 hour.
- Snapshot integrity check: 100% of snapshots must pass signature verification and manifest consistency checks on write.
- Retention enforcement: TEA bundles must be retained for at least 3 years by default (configurable per-customer or per-region).

Ownership and Roles:

- Evidence Owner: Security (primary) — Responsible for policy, signature key lifecycle, and evidence release decisions.
- Snapshot Service Team: Eng-infra — Implements snapshot exporters, signing pipeline, storage lifecycle.
- Compliance & Legal: Reviews retention parameters and approves redaction rules.
- Customer Success / Support: Handles evidence requests from customers and coordinates redaction where necessary.

High-level TEA Workflow (numbered steps):

1. Event capture: All identity changes are recorded in the canonical change-log (SCIM webhook stream, SSO audit events, internal role-binding service events).
2. Materialization: Every 24 hours (or more frequently when configured) the Snapshot Service materializes a point-in-time view by applying ordered change-log events up to timestamp T to the authoritative model.
3. Normalization: The materialized state is normalized to a canonical JSON schema (see "Data Model" below).
4. Signing & Manifest: The normalized JSON is hashed (SHA-256), signed with the TEA signing key (KMS-backed), and a manifest is produced containing checksums, key id, generation timestamp, and provenance pointers to raw change events.
5. Bundle composition: The signed snapshot is packaged with: compressed raw audit events (within window), relevant ACL/role-definition versions, and a provenance index.
6. Immutable storage: The bundle is uploaded to the immutable evidence store with lifecycle rules and cross-region replication as required by policy.
7. Access & delivery: Evidence requests produce an audit trail; bundles are exported to authorized requesters with an access token and release justification.

Data Model (canonical snapshot JSON, described in prose):

- Top-level fields: snapshot_id (content-hash), generated_at (RFC3339), effective_at (RFC3339), generator_version, signing_key_id.
- Principals array: each entry contains principal_id (opaque GUID), principal_type (user/service/oauth-client), display_name, hashed_email (sha256) when required by privacy rules, active_roles: [{role_id, role_version, assignment_type, assigned_at, expires_at}].
- Roles array: role_id, role_name, role_definition_version, permissions_hash.
- Provenance index: list of source events (event_id, source_system, recorded_at, checksum) used to reconstruct the snapshot.

Retention & Redaction Policy (table described in text):

- By default: TEA bundles retained 3 years; move to archive tier after 1 year; delete only via approved retention purge workflow.
- Sensitive identifiers (email, phone): store hashed unless explicit legal/incident justification exists.
- Regional override: For regions with stricter data residency, generate snapshot copies constrained to region and store per-region evidence store.

(Example retention schedule)
- 0-1 year: hot access in evidence-store-primary, full contents
- 1-3 years: cold archival with read-only access, logs compressed
- >3 years: Purge only by legal-approved retention purge task

Audit Logging Integration:

- Every snapshot generation MUST emit a "snapshot.generated" audit event with fields: snapshot_id, effective_at, generator_version, signer_key_id, upload_location.
- Snapshot verification endpoint: /api/internal/teas/{snapshot_id}/verify must return {ok: true, signer_key: <keyid>, signature_valid: true} when validated.
- Example audit event (JSON):

{
  "event_type": "snapshot.generated",
  "snapshot_id": "sha256:abcd...",
  "effective_at": "2028-05-14T00:00:00Z",
  "generated_at": "2028-05-14T00:15:02Z",
  "generated_by": "snapshot-service-v1.7.3",
  "uploader": "evidence-uploader-fn-03",
  "signer_key_id": "projects/redwood-kms/keys/tea-signing-v2"
}

Evidence Request and Release Playbook (step-by-step):

1. Request intake: Request must include requester identity, justification, scope (date/time range, principals), and confidentiality level.
2. Pre-flight checks: Compliance validates retention window and redaction scope; Security verifies request cause (audit/legal/incident).
3. Generation: If snapshot exists for requested point-in-time, fetch; otherwise trigger on-demand generation.
4. Review & redaction: Produce a candidate bundle; redact hashed fields as per policy. Legal may request full identifiers for active investigations (audit trail required).
5. Release: Sign an evidence-release record, provision temporary access token (12-hour), and log release event (snapshot.released).

Incident Response: Entitlement Compromise Scenario (brief playbook):

- Triage: Security triggers TEA immediate snapshot with pre- and post-compromise windows (T-24h, T, T+24h).
- Immutable evidence lock: Mark impacted snapshots as "forensic-locked" — no lifecycle deletion or automatic archiving while lock is active.
- Correlation: Use provenance index to correlate role changes to deployment events, SSO logins, and API key rotations.
- Escalation: If evidence shows unauthorized elevation, initiate emergency deprovisioning runbooks and notify affected customers per contractual obligations.

Verification and Audit Checklist (short checklist):

- [ ] Snapshot ID is content-hash and signature verifies with KMS key id in manifest.
- [ ] Provenance index references the source audit events used.
- [ ] Region and retention policy applied correctly to stored bundle.
- [ ] Release record and requester justification captured in access logs.
- [ ] For incident bundles: forensic-lock set and documented.

Implementation Notes and Examples:

- Command to generate a snapshot (example CLI):

redwood-tea generate --effective-at 2028-05-14T00:00:00Z --output /tmp/tea-2028-05-14.tar.gz --sign-with projects/redwood-kms/keys/tea-signing-v2

- Minimal verification curl example:

curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.local/api/internal/teas/sha256:abcd.../verify | jq

- SQL example to assemble active roles for a user at time T (conceptual):

-- returns role assignments active at time T
SELECT principal_id, role_id, assigned_at, expires_at
FROM rbac_role_assignments
WHERE assigned_at <= TIMESTAMP '2028-05-14 00:00:00'
  AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > TIMESTAMP '2028-05-14 00:00:00');

Operational considerations and risks:

- Storage growth: TEA bundles are large if snapshots include raw events; use deduplication and incremental deltas by default.
- Key management: Rotate TEA signing keys annually; maintain previous keys for verification with key meta in manifest.
- Legal holds: Ensure evidence purge operations respect active legal holds; implement pre-check hooks for purge tasks.

Rollout Plan (phased):

1. Pilot: Enable TEA for a single critical tenant and internal service accounts for 3 months.
2. Expand: Enable daily snapshots for all production tenants; add cross-region replication where required.
3. Hardening: Add on-demand generation, verification endpoint, and integration with case-management (legal/incidents).

Appendices:

- Appendix A: Canonical JSON schema (link noted in related_pages).
- Appendix B: Mapping matrix of source systems -> snapshot fields (SSO audit, SCIM, internal bindings).
- Appendix C: FAQ and common redaction requests.

This guideline should be reviewed annually and after any major IAM or audit-logging changes.
